## Roles to bind (domain: finance)
- journal: The transactional ledger of record: one row per posting line, carrying a signed amount and a document reference; debit and credit lines balance per document.
- amount_local: The signed posting amount in its transaction or functional currency.
- doc_ref: The document or voucher reference grouping posting lines into one accounting document.
- account: The account or cost-category identifier used to decide whether a posting belongs in vessel build cost.
- period: The accounting period to which a posting belongs at fiscal-period granularity.
- entity: The legal entity or company code to whose books a posting belongs.
- build_ref: The reference attributing a posting to one vessel build after resolution through the approved build-identity mapping.
- currency: The currency in which the local posting amount is denominated.
- amount_reporting_currency: The posting amount translated into the confirmed group reporting currency using the approved translation policy, kept distinct from the as-posted local amount.
- source_system: The originating ledger, interface or manual-entry channel retained for posted-versus-adjusted reconciliation.
- approval_status: The workflow status showing whether the posting was approved for use in the relevant cost view.
- invoice_ref: The supplier-invoice reference used with other evidence to identify duplicate or reversing cost postings.
- purchase_order_ref: The purchasing reference used with invoice, supplier and amount evidence to attribute and deduplicate build costs.
- subledger_ar: The accounts-receivable open items: one row per open receivable with a signed amount, reconcilable against the journal's control account.
- intercompany: Paired intercompany resource charges between legal entities whose sender and receiver sides must reconcile before group build cost can retain the underlying resource cost once and eliminate internal markup.
- ic_build_ref: The vessel build to which an intercompany resource charge is attributable after approved identity resolution.
- ic_seller_entity: The legal entity providing the intercompany resource or service.
- ic_buyer_entity: The legal entity receiving the intercompany resource or service.
- ic_cost_base: The underlying resource cost before intercompany markup.
- ic_markup_rate: The markup applied to the intercompany cost base under the applicable transfer-pricing policy.
- ic_sender_ref: The sender-side document reference used to pair an intercompany charge.
- ic_receiver_ref: The receiver-side document reference used to pair an intercompany charge.
- ic_match_status: The reconciliation state of the sender, receiver and elimination records for an intercompany charge.
- build: One governed vessel-construction undertaking, including its approved identity, aliases and lifecycle state, to which costs can be attributed.
- authoritative_key: The owner-confirmed stable business identifier for one vessel build.
- alias_set: The approved set of alternate project, yard-job, contract and vessel references that identify the same build.
- completion_status: The governed lifecycle state distinguishing accepted or delivered builds, work in progress, and cancelled or pre-contract activity.
- acceptance_date: The effective date on which the completed vessel was accepted under the confirmed completion policy.
- forecast_cost_reporting_currency: The latest approved estimate of total cost at completion in the group reporting currency, distinct from cost incurred to date.
- labour_allocation: An approved allocation of labour effort and burdened cost to a vessel build, including allocations not yet interfaced to the journal.
- labour_build_ref: The vessel build receiving the labour allocation after approved alias resolution.
- labour_period: The period in which the allocated labour was performed.
- labour_cost_reporting_currency: The approved burdened labour cost in the group reporting currency.
- labour_approval_status: The workflow state establishing whether the allocation is approved for accrual or posting.
- labour_source_ref: The stable source reference used to reconcile an allocation to its journal posting and prevent duplicate accrual.
- overhead_pool: A governed pool of indirect production cost eligible for allocation to vessel builds under a confirmed allocation policy.
- overhead_location: The operating location whose indirect production cost forms the pool.
- overhead_period: The fiscal period for which the overhead pool is measured.
- overhead_pool_amount: The eligible indirect production cost amount before allocation to builds.
- overhead_allocation_base: The owner-approved driver used to allocate the pool consistently across builds.
- overhead_base_quantity: The measured quantity of the approved allocation driver for a pool or receiving build.
